# HEM v0.6.1b18 — Retire the obsolete device-wide controller method

- **Only per-operating-mode controller methods:** Heating, Cooling, Drying, Humidifying, Fan and genuinely supported modes have their own independent PID/Automatic/Manual/Existing/Off selections. One physical controller continues to arbitrate device commands safely.
- **Remove the legacy entity, not just its card:** HEM no longer registers the old device-wide `Control method` selector. At integration setup it removes its exact registry unique ID, even when the Home Assistant entity has been renamed. The retired selector no longer appears in the card or the categorized HEM device settings dialog.
- **Preserve existing control on upgrade:** previously saved global method values are not wiped or implicitly changed during this migration. Per-mode settings continue to resolve existing saved values until the mode is explicitly edited; no automatic hardware action is triggered by retirement.
- **No silent fallback dropdown:** if a device cannot supply a verified operating mode, HEM does not recreate the legacy control. The device remains subject to normal availability and safe-mode checks until its native capabilities are known.
- **Scope and safety:** no change to physical controller IDs, mode arbitration, PID math, minimum ON/OFF intervals, pending command history, device ownership, physical services, or authorization.
- **Verification:** an exact-identity retirement test confirms that unrelated integration entities and the mode-specific selectors are left alone, and real Chromium tests verify the absence of the legacy dropdown even on legacy-only fixtures.

Install through HACS/Marketplace. Restart Home Assistant to complete entity-registry migration and reload the HEM Lovelace card.
